title: Every counterparty is enabled by Sky Governance writing per-venue configuration into the controller
content:
Reading the admin functions as a set (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.1) reveals a consistent shape. Every one writes into a **mapping keyed by counterparty**: `maxSlippages[pool]`, `uniswapV3PoolParams[pool]`, `maxExchangeRates[token]`, `mintRecipients[destinationDomain]`, `layerZeroRecipients[destinationEndpointId]`, `centrifugeRecipients[centrifugeId]`. Add the token-keyed rate limits that double as the whitelist (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.2.1.2), and the controller holds **no global configuration at all** — only per-venue entries.

The consequence is that a new venue is unusable until governance populates its keys, and every safety bound is specific to that venue rather than inherited from a default. There is no "permissive by default" state to be caught out by: an unconfigured pool has a zero allowance, no recipient, and no permitted tick range.

Because `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` is "fully controlled by Sky Governance via the Grove Proxy" (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.1.1), this means **Sky Governance — not Grove Governance — writes every one of these entries**. Grove decides how to trade inside the envelope; Sky decides what the envelope is, venue by venue.

That closes a loop with the governance layer. A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.2.1 requires a new Allocation System Instance to go through Root Edit, and A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.4 adds a Core Council Risk Advisor gate for risk-increasing changes. The onchain configuration model **enforces** that document-level requirement rather than merely restating it: without the corresponding admin writes, an Instance approved on paper cannot transact.

The cost is latency. Every parameter tune — a slippage cap that is too tight, a TWAP window that is too short — waits on a Sky Executive Vote, which is a poor fit for market conditions that change hourly.
description: Slippage caps, tick bounds, TWAP windows, exchange-rate ceilings, bridge recipients and rate limits are all keyed by pool or token and writable only by the admin role Sky Governance holds.
